findings.text: a second collapse of a section that is already collapsed returns ok true and writes a nested card: the replacement runs from the inner h2 to the next structured-state region, so the first card's closing header and section tags and its landed-summary paragraph are consumed, the first landing's summary and its evidence link are destroyed, the outer wrapper is left unclosed, and the document then fails reckon audit-doc with exit 1 (section-unclosed); a coordinator re-running a landing beat to refresh a summary or anchor, or a retried write, therefore lands corruption silently.

the tests line of the reviewed manifest and its after_suite command field carry the literal placeholder PYTHONPATH=<tree> where the contract asks for the command that actually ran, so the command is recoverable only from the gate log's own header and not from the record a reader is given.

item_verdicts.manifest: read at the reviewed head; it names the three commits, both gate arms with their logs, the reviewed write paths and the declared mutation, and its evidence fragment reproduces the log summaries I read back from the logs themselves (20 passed base, 25 passed after, 1 failed mutant).
